steps.name: Sample structure QC incl. shallow sample_01 adjudication
caveats: Do not delete the low-depth sample silently: count models down-weight it through its size factor, so removal is a judgment, not a default.

The profile does not say whether Salmon length correction was applied. If the count matrix contains fractional entries, report the fraction of fractional entries in the QC output so the import state is documented before the DESeq2 model is built.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-signature-scores-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, gene-level Salmon counts as delivered, length-correction state not recorded) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-signature-scores-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (columns: sample, condition; 6 inflamed, 6 control; unpaired, single batch). Organism: human (Homo sapiens). Known quality concern: sample_01 library size ~4x below the study median.
steps.question: Do the 12 ileum samples (6 Crohn disease inflamed vs 6 control per metadata.csv) structure by condition, and does sample_01 - library size about 4x below the median - carry enough information to stay in the analysis?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: blind vst, PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf; shallow sample_01 kept, inspected, and reported per R-0008@440d.

constraints: Apply the variance-stabilizing transformation blind to the design (transform=vst_blind) and run PCA on the 500 most variable genes (n_top_genes=500).
Draw a heatmap of Euclidean distances between samples, colored by condition (low_depth_policy=keep_inspect_report).
Report a per-sample table of library size and detected-gene count for all 12 samples, sample_01 alongside the others.

Give an explicit keep/drop verdict for sample_01: keep by default; drop only with a stated reason visible in the QC (e.g. separated from its condition in PCA, suspected identity problem) - never for depth alone.
Write out the approved sample set (all 12, or 11 with the stated reason) as the only sample set downstream steps may use.
steps.description: Blind-vst PCA, sample-distance heatmap, and per-sample depth/detection table that adjudicate the shallow sample_01 and fix the sample set for the run.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot, sample-distance heatmap, and per-sample library-size/detected-gene table are produced and saved.
sample_01 has an explicit keep/drop verdict with a stated reason.
The approved sample set is written out and is consumed by every downstream step.

steps.name: Low count filter + size-factor normalization for scoring
caveats: A depth difference alone does not bias size-factor-corrected values: the low-depth sample carries less information (wider intervals), which is correct model behavior (R-0030).
Do not rescale the matrix after size factors are applied - scoring must consume model-consistent log-normalized values.
steps.context: Uses only the sample set approved in T1S1. Counts as delivered from Salmon (length-correction state unknown). Smallest group size = 6 (Crohn disease inflamed, 6 samples). Organism: human.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 delivered genes carry enough counts to support stable signature scoring, and what is the log2-normalized, size-factor-adjusted expression matrix the scorer consumes?

grounding.reason: Low count filter (>=10 counts in >= smallest group size) per R-0002@087b; normalization inside the model with median-of-ratios size factors per R-0026@9ab1; depth handled by size factors per R-0030@2248. The template's DE test is not run - not requested.

constraints: Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples, 6 (min_count=10, min_samples=smallest_group_size).

Normalize with DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors (size_factors=median_of_ratios_named_in_the_plan); size factors account for depth (depth_policy=size_factors_account_for_depth). Do not scale, transform, or normalize the counts before the model.
Produce a log2-normalized expression matrix (DESeq2 rlog or vst on the filtered matrix) as the scoring input (input_scale=log_normalized_expression).
Do not run a gene-level differential expression test - it is out of scope for this run.
Report genes kept out of 12000, the per-sample size factors (explicitly including sample_01), and confirm the matrix is non-negative; if entries are fractional, report the fraction.
steps.description: DESeq2 low-count pre-filter and median-of-ratios size factors, exporting the log2-normalized matrix that the signature scorer consumes.
acceptance_criteria: Filtered count matrix and log2-normalized matrix are written out, with a gene-count summary.
Per-sample size factors are reported, including sample_01.
The log-normalized matrix contains exactly the approved sample set from T1S1.

plan.title: Crohn's ileum hallmark signature scores, inflamed vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a per-sample signature readout: score every one of the 50 human MSigDB Hallmark sets in each of the 12 ileum samples (6 Crohn's inflamed, 6 control), then test which scores separate the two groups. The Salmon count table (12000 genes x 12 samples; length-correction state not recorded) goes through three pre-scoring stages. First, sample-structure QC that explicitly adjudicates sample_01, whose library size is about 4x below the median: keep, inspect, and report it rather than drop it silently, removing it only with a stated reason. Second, a low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples) and DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, which account for the shallow sample's depth, producing the log2-normalized matrix. Third, rank-based within-sample UCell scoring of the 50 Hallmark sets on that matrix, so depth cannot distort any sample's score. The 50 x N score matrix is tested with limma under the same two-group design, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the 50 signatures, and the group test is repeated without sample_01 so the report states which signatures depend on the shallow replicate. A final report bundles the QC verdict, the score matrix, and the differential tables with a full reproducibility record.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST sample structure QC: PCA on 500 top-variance genes + sample distance heatmap
UCell rank-based per-sample scores; limma on score matrix with the condition design; BH across signatures

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.
